'''Monta Jerome Ellis''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|m|ɒ|n|t|eɪ}} {{respell|MON|tay}}; born October 26, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Ellis attended [[Lanier High School (Jackson, Mississippi)|Lanier High School]] in [[Jackson, Mississippi]], where he was a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and first-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]]. He entered the [[NBA]] directly out of high school, being drafted with the 40th overall pick by the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the [[2005 NBA draft]]. In 2007, he was named the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|NBA Most Improved Player]]. During his career Ellis was one of the best scorers in the league, averaging close to 25 points per game on two occasions.

After six and a half seasons with Golden State, he was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in March 2012; a season and a half with the Bucks was followed by two seasons with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] and finally, two seasons with the [[Indiana Pacers]].

'''Mitchell Leon Butler''' (born December 15, 1970) is an American [[sports agent]] and former professional [[basketball]] player. He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) from 1993 to 2004.

The {{convert|6|ft|5|in|m|adj=on}} [[shooting guard]] signed [[NBA draft|undrafted]] with the [[Washington Bullets]] in 1993 after a collegiate career at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] in which he played in more career games than any other Bruin and swiped the seventh-most steals in UCLA history. After three seasons in Washington, Butler was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] along with [[Rasheed Wallace]] in exchange for [[Rod Strickland]] and [[Harvey Grant]]. Following his stint playing for the Blazers, he signed as a free agent with the Cleveland Cavaliers. Following the [[1998–99 NBA season|1999 season]], Butler did not play in the NBA for two years. In [[2001–02 NBA season|2001–02]], Butler signed with the Trail Blazers, marking his second stint with the franchise. Mitchell's last year in the league was in the [[2003–04 NBA season|2003–04 season]], when he once again played for the D.C. franchise, now renamed the Washington Wizards. Butler played in a total of 362 NBA games with 33 starts. He owns career averages of 5.2 points, 2 rebounds, and 1 assist.

Butler appeared in the 1994 movie ''[[Blue Chips]]''.

Butler worked as NBA sports agent with [[Lagardère Unlimited]] before joining Rival Sports Group as president of basketball.<ref>{{cite news|last=Mullen |first=Liz |title=Butler, formerly of Lagardère, takes position as president of basketball for Rival Sports Group |date=March 19, 2014 |work=sportsbusinessdaily.com |url=http://www.sportsbusinessdaily.com/Journal/Issues/2014/05/19/Labor-and-Agents/Mitchell-Butler.aspx |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140521070439/https://www.sportsbusinessdaily.com/Journal/Issues/2014/05/19/Labor-and-Agents/Mitchell-Butler.aspx |archivedate=May 21, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''Maurice Williams''' (born December 19, 1982) is an assistant men's [[basketball]] coach at the [[University of Kentucky]] and a former professional [[basketball]] player who played 13 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). After two seasons at Alabama, Williams entered the [[2003 NBA draft]] where he was selected with the 47th overall pick by the [[Utah Jazz]]. Throughout his career, he has also played for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], [[Charlotte Hornets]] and [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. In [[2009 NBA All-Star Game|2009]], Williams was selected as an [[NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star]]. In the [[2016 NBA Finals]], he won his only NBA championship with the Cavaliers. He retired as a player in 2017.

In May 2018, Williams became an assistant coach for the [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball]] team. In May 2020, he became the head coach for the [[Alabama State Hornets basketball]] team, but stayed for just two seasons before resigning in March 2022. A few days later he was named head coach at [[Jackson State University]] in his home town, replacing [[Wayne Brent]]. On March 30, 2026, Williams was hired as an assistant coach at the [[University of Kentucky]].

'''Miloš Teodosić''' ({{lang-sr-cyr|Милош Теодосић}}, born March 19, 1987) is a Serbian former professional [[basketball]] player. He also represented the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|National Basketball Team of Serbia]] internationally. He primarily played the [[point guard]] and [[shooting guard]] positions. He is a six time [[All-EuroLeague]] selection, and was voted [[EuroLeague MVP]] in [[Euroleague 2009–10|2010]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Milos-Teodosic | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140804005908/http://www.fiba.com/basketballworldcup/2014/Milos-TEODOSIC | url-status = live | archive-date = August 4, 2014 | title = TEODOSIĆ, Miloš | publisher = FIBA.com | access-date = August 18, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=JDR | title = TEODOSIĆ, Miloš | publisher = EUROLEAGUE.net | access-date = August 18, 2015}}</ref>

Under Teodosić the Serbia national team won a [[EuroBasket]] silver medal in [[EuroBasket 2009|2009]], as well as a [[FIBA Basketball World Cup]] silver medal in [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2014]], being elected to the All-Tournament Team in both competitions. He also won an Olympic silver medal at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Rio Games]].<ref>[https://archive.today/20160819122714/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp/150/q/Milos%20TEODOSIC/pid/44167/_//players.html FIBA.com profile]</ref> He was named [[FIBA Europe Men's Player of the Year Award|FIBA Europe Player of the Year]] in 2010, and in 2016, he was voted the best non-NBA player in the world by NBA coaches,<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.opencourt-basketball.com/milos-teodosic-the-best-non-nba-player-in-the-world/|title=Milos Teodosic – The Best Non NBA Player in the World|last=Peters|first=Damien|date=October 24, 2016|newspaper=Opencourt Basketball|access-date=November 22, 2016}}</ref> as well as the [[Euroscar|European Player of the Year]] by ''[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Basket/16-01-2017/basket-euro-player-2016-teodosic-nba-battuta-16-anni-180435253039.shtml |title=Basket, Euro Player 2016 a Teodosic: Nba battuta dopo 16 anni | newspaper=La Gazzetta dello Sport |date=January 16, 2017 |access-date=January 16, 2017|language=it}}</ref>

'''Mirza Teletović''' (born September 18, 1985) is a Bosnian former professional [[basketball]] player who was the president of the [[Basketball Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina]] from 2018 to 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.klix.ba/sport/kosarka/mirza-teletovic-podnio-ostavku-na-mjesto-predsjednika-kosarkaskog-saveza-bih/220608048|title=Mirza Teletović podnio ostavku na mjesto predsjednika Košarkaškog saveza BiH|date=June 8, 2022|access-date=June 8, 2022|language=bs|author=E.B.|publisher=Klix.ba}}</ref> As a player, he spent six seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He also represented and [[Captain (sports)|captain]]ed the [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national basketball team]]. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=9}}, he played at the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position.

Teletović started his career in Bosnia with [[KK Sloboda Tuzla|Sloboda Tuzla]], which was followed by a stint in Belgium with [[BC Oostende|Oostende]]. He played six years for [[Saski Baskonia]], with whom he won two [[Liga ACB]] championships. He was also named to the [[All-ACB Team]] in 2012. Then, he played five seasons in the NBA for the [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[Phoenix Suns]] and [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. On September 27, 2018, Teletović announced his retirement after suffering a career-ending [[pulmonary embolism]] injury during his tenure with the Bucks and then got waived in March 2018, removing his final year of his contract in December of that same year.
